doc.title: Bobby Shew interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 1, 2020

title: Leadership qualities of bandleaders; Benny Goodman's treatment of Buddy Tate
summary: Asked about leaders he admired or resented, Shew calls Goodman the most difficult and describes his racist treatment of Buddy Tate.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Did you have, with the big bands you played with which included Woody Herman and Goodman and Toshiko and Louie Bellson, did they have — did any of them have leadership qualities that you either resented or admired?
Okay you don’t get away with just a yes now.

Yeah all of them had — I think the biggest idiot that I ever worked for and one of the most difficult people, and I’m not the only person who would tell you this, this has been written up in books, was Benny Goodman. He was an extremely difficult person, I think even his daughter I remember in an interview, never understood her father. He was like I don’t know, in those days we didn’t know what the term “bipolar” meant you know. It was not a term that was around. I would guess almost that Benny had some bipolar things or some schizophrenia thing. Because you could never quite figure out why he had to be so nasty and so mean and so condescending to people. Like when people had words with him he was racist — I remember Buddy Tate, one time when Buddy Tate was on the band and I was there and he sent Buddy out like he was like a slave. He sent him out, he called him “boy” all the time and it was like embarrassing. You know? It was like I mean
Buddy was such a — nicest cat in the world and a great player. Why is Benny treating him like that? I thought God this is insane.
You know Joe Wilder would not even say his name.
